title: Service workers and offline caching strategies

videos.script:
Lesson 9's caches are the browser's, and they follow the server's headers. {{between}} A service worker is a cache you write: a script that sits between the page and the network, sees every request the page makes, and decides for each one where the answer comes from.

{{strategies}} You will write the planner's: three strategies, one for each kind of file. Hashed files from the cache first. Pages from the network first, and the last copy when the network is gone. Fonts and pictures from the cache at once, refreshed behind the visitor's back.

{{offline}} Then you will take the browser off the network and open the planner. The course you visited opens. A course you never visited says so, politely, instead of the browser's error. {{update}} And last, the part that catches everybody: how a new version of a service worker replaces the old one, and why it waits.
